sections: The holding's own list of values
read.role: reads each row's figure at the price at that row's own date

recordType.value: rate, with plaintext account_id empty, AES-256-GCM under the vault DEK like every other record

noPlaintextSymbolOrDate.value: there is no plaintext symbol column and no plaintext date column. The symbol stays inside the ciphertext, because a durable table of (principal, symbol, date, rate) rows is the list of what a person holds

recordIdDerivation.value: a random UUIDv4. Deriving it from the symbol and the date would let the server compute the id for every symbol in its own table and match

payloadShape.value: { symbol, date, rate, rateTarget, rateSource, rateAsOf, proposedRate }

dateFormat.value: YYYY-MM-DD, no time and no timezone. It is the date the price applies to, which is the date the entry was recorded at, not the date the entry was written

rateArithmetic.value: decimal string at scale 12, parsed and computed as BigInt, no IEEE-754 float at any point. A rate with more than twelve decimal places is rejected at input rather than truncated

rateTarget.value: the ISO 4217 code rate converts into, which is the main currency as of entry time, written into every entry

rateAsOfRule.value: the date the provider's figure actually applies to, which may lag date. null when manual. For edited it keeps the proposal's date

proposedRateRule.value: set exactly when rateSource is edited and null otherwise, and it records the original proposal, so editing an edited rate a second time leaves it alone

uniqueness.value: one entry per (symbol, date), and one record per entry. Not one record per symbol holding its whole series and not one record per date holding every symbol

refreshSymbolSet.value: the distinct unit of every active account, minus any unit equal to the profile's mainCurrency. An archived account's symbol is not refreshed, except that a moved entry's own unit is always among them, so an archived holding's entry moved to an earlier date is priced there too

archivingIsRecording.value: archiving is recording: its zero refreshes the archive date like any quantity, written while the holding is still active so its unit is among the symbols. Ensure semantics apply: a date whose prices are complete asks the proxy nothing and rewrites no entry. The last active holding measured in a unit, once archived, stops that unit being refreshed and keeps its entries

mainCurrencyRate.value: 1 by definition, stored nowhere and requested from nobody

refreshDate.value: the date of the entry being written, the sweep's date, the single-holding form's date or the date a moved entry lands on, never today

refreshCardinality.value: at most one refresh per recording date, ensured once for the whole sitting, so a fifteen-row sweep writes one set of prices and issues one rate request

refreshTrigger.value: recording a quantity refreshes. Reopening a recording does not. Recording a quantity means a quantity arriving at a date it was not at: a new figure, a figure added for a holding skipped at a past date, and an entry moved onto another date. Changing a figure or a note where it stands, changing a rate, or clearing a figure is not recording a quantity and ensures nothing. The refresh is an ensure over the date, so running it twice is a no-op the second time

movedEntryRefresh.value: moving a snapshot's date ensures the new date's prices, covering the moved entry's own unit, and writes an entry only for a symbol the new date has none for. With the new date's prices complete it issues no request to /api/rates. No stored price is rewritten and the date the entry left keeps every one of its prices. When the source gives no answer nothing is written for that symbol, the entry still moves, and it reads not priced at the new date, never at the price of the date it left or any earlier one

moveWriteOrder.value: the snapshot PUT, then every rate PUT, then the displaced record's DELETE. The quantity gates the prices. A failed rate PUT skips nothing after it, the DELETE still runs, and the dialog reports the entry moved and names each symbol whose price did not land

rateSourceAtADate.value: a symbol has a rate source at a date when its row in the symbol table carries lookup: true and the date is on or after the later of the row's since and the main currency's row's since. Free text, a lookup: false symbol, and any symbol at a date before that have none. The main currency is always a kind: currency row, so its since is set whatever its lookup. A main currency retired since registration is absent from the client's table and bounds nothing there, while the server still applies its floor, so on dates before 1999-01-04, or 2000-01-13 for the currencies that start then, that vault's lines read as a source that did not answer. That is accepted. The client computes it from the table it already holds, with no request. This one test decides the price at a date, whether a recording asks the proxy about the symbol, and whether the line offers Look it up

priceAtADate.value: values a figure shown at its own date: a recording's figures, a holding's own list of values, and the converted figure on the sweep and the single-holding form wherever the unit's rate line for that date holds no figure. With a rate source at that date (rateSourceAtADate) it is the entry at exactly that date and no other, else not priced. Without one (free text, lookup: false, or a date before the later of the since values) it is the entry with the greatest date at or before that date, and when that entry's date is earlier than the figure's the figure carries the entry's date; with no entry at or before the date, not priced. Before a symbol's since its own entries are estimates like the flat's: a 2012 gold figure takes the person's last gold price at or before it, with that price's date. A flagged pair is no entry at its date. A unit equal to mainCurrency is exactly 1 with no date

lookupIsIssuedOnlyWhenNeeded.value: a rate request is issued only when a symbol the date needs has no entry at it and has a rate source at that date, which is why opening an old recording is silent, an empty rate line included, and why a date whose only missing symbols have no rate source there asks the proxy nothing

lookItUp.value: on a reopened recording, Look it up is offered on a line with no entry at the date whose symbol has a rate source at that date (rateSourceAtADate), and on no other line. An XAU-g line with no entry at 2012-12-31 does not offer it. Pressing it issues exactly one request to /api/rates, for that date, shows the answer as a proposal carrying its rateAsOf, and writes nothing until the rate-lines save. The action, not the act of opening, issues the request

noProposalCases.value: no proposal and a previous entry exists means nothing is written and the previous entry stays the latest, at its own date. No rate source at that date (free text, a lookup: false symbol, or a date before the symbol's since) means nothing is written unless the person edits it, and re-dating an unreviewed estimate is refused. No entry yet and no proposal means the row asks for the price and the holding stays unpriced, and the quantity still saves

dateBeforeSince.value: a date before a symbol's since (gold in 2012) behaves as a free-text unit's line: it starts from the newest entry before the date, writes nothing unless changed, and writes a typed figure as manual. No request asks about it, a reopened recording offers no Look it up on it, and its line never carries the wording of a source that did not answer. With no entry at or before the date, the line asks for a price when a quantity in that unit is recorded

dateBeforeSinceCopyDate.value: the sweep's line names the date published prices begin, which is the later of the unit's first published date and the main currency's, written as Settings sets dates and always with its year. The unit, the dates and the main currency are computed, not written into the copy. The three sentences (price set earlier, price set on the day, no price at or before) are the screen's own

editedRateNeverLeavesTheBrowser.value: an edited rate is not part of, and does not trigger, any request to /api/rates, in any field, in any encoding

writeOrderFreshRecording.value: the quantity PUT goes first and its result is the row's result. On success the recording date's price entries are PUT, one request each, starting with the symbol of the row just written. A price write cannot fail a quantity write and a price write failure is never silent

writeOrderEditedRecording.value: a reopened recording is saved one control at a time and no save spans a quantity, rates and deletions at once. A row's save writes that holding's quantity alone: an update, a create with the pre-create reload and the refresh behind it, or the deletion of a cleared figure. The rate-lines save runs 0 the pre-create reload if any line creates an entry, 1 rate writes creates and updates alike, 2 deletions for the lines cleared. A phase's requests may be issued together and the next phase begins when every request in the previous one has answered. No step is skipped because an earlier one failed

typedRateIsUngated.value: at a date that holds a record, a rate the person typed does not wait on a quantity, so the rate-lines save needs no holding touched alongside it and triggers no refresh. A refreshed entry is still gated behind a successful quantity write

typedPriceAtADateHoldingNoRecord.value: at a date holding no record, nothing is written until the first quantity is. That quantity's success writes the refresh and every typed price with it, each typed figure in its proposal's place with the rateSource Record shape gives it, so the date gets all its prices in one go. Order is the quantity PUT first, then the rate entries. From then on the date holds a recording and the rate-lines save is offered as on a reopened one, however the sweep was entered

noRateLinesSaveAtAnEmptyDate.value: the sweep shows no rate-lines save control at a date holding no record, and the client's rate-lines write refuses at such a date, checked against the model in memory, before any request: it issues no request and writes nothing. Two checks, because the control being absent is not the refusal

dateEmptiedWhileWorking.value: when another window deleted the recording before a rate-lines save, the save is refused before anything is written, and the screen reloads to a date holding nothing: every row reads as nothing recorded, the rate block has no save, and what was typed stays on the lines and in the rows. A Callout under the date heading, carrying the critical icon, reads 'Another window deleted the recording for 31 July. Your prices were not saved. They are still here and are saved with the first holding you record for this date.', the date computed. The typed prices then go in with the first row recorded (typedPriceAtADateHoldingNoRecord)

detection.value: a rate-lines save that creates an entry learns of the deletion from its pre-create reload (step 0). When the reloaded date holds no snapshot and no rate, the whole save is refused before any write, the model takes the reloaded records, and every typed price stays on screen

typedPriceNeverMakesARecording.value: a typed price alone never creates a recording, so a recording holding only rate entries is always one the person emptied (cleared, deleted or moved away every quantity). Leaving first writes nothing, no PUT and no DELETE, and the screen landed on names each unit whose typed price was left unsaved

versionRules.value: the refresh only ever creates, at version 1. Somebody editing a stored entry updates it at stored version + 1. A Conflict is surfaced and never retried: the line reloads to what is stored and the message names the symbol

partialSaveReporting.value: the screen stays open, every change keeps its own state, the message names which changes were saved and which were not, by symbol, while a row reports on itself, a retry reissues only what failed at whatever version each record now holds, and the in-memory model advances per write. Nothing in the vault records that a save was partial: no pending flag and no dirty marker

duplicateHandling.value: two entries for one (symbol, date) whose decrypted payloads are byte-identical in every field are deleted down to one. Anything else is rendered in that date's recording, flagged, with an action to keep one, and the pair drops out of the symbol's series until then. There is no provenance ranking and no automatic winner

readingDefinitions.value: the latest price for a symbol is the entry with the greatest date, never the most recently written. The price as recorded for an account is the entry with the greatest date at or before the date of that account's latest quantity entry, whatever its symbol. A unit equal to mainCurrency prices at exactly 1, from no entry, and is not an unpriced holding

editingRules.value: a stored price is edited inside the recording for its date and nowhere else. rate, rateSource and rateAsOf open on the stored values, never on a fresh proposal, and opening a recording fetches no proposal at all. Editing by hand moves proposed to edited and captures the replaced figure as proposedRate, leaving rateAsOf unchanged

editConfirmation.value: editing one entry changes every holding measured in that symbol on that date, and the confirmation says so, naming how many holdings are affected. The count is of holdings whose value on that date actually changes: measured in that unit, not archived before the date, holding a figure at or before it, and whose quantity on that date is not zero. A holding archived earlier, first valued later, or at zero that day, the archive's zero included, is not counted. A save changing several rates confirms once, naming each symbol and its count

deletionEffect.value: deleting an entry is allowed by clearing its line, and every entry at a date goes together when the recording itself is deleted. The confirmation says that figures around that date will change, and, when the entry is the symbol's only one, that every holding measured in it becomes unpriced

provenanceChips.value: proposed renders as 'Market rate', or 'Market rate as of 29 Jul' where the provider's figure is for an earlier day. edited renders as 'Edited from 0.931200', naming the figure that was replaced as editable writes it (ratePriceFigure). manual renders as 'Typed by you'. The same three words are used wherever a price's origin is shown, the sweep's rate block included

ratePriceFigure.value: a rate is written through the formatter's editable(value, places) at six places, wherever one is written: in its field, in the note naming the figure an edit replaced, beside a rival entry, and in a recording's price column. Every digit of the exact value is kept, never rounded, and the fraction is padded to at least six, grouped and pointed as configured. It does not follow moneyPlaces. The reverse is parseFigure, which returns the exact value at scale 12 or nothing

ratePriceFigureExamples.value: 0.797 writes 0.797000 and 0.9312 writes 0.931200. A proposal at eight places writes all eight, so "0.12345678" reads 0.12345678. With locale de-DE and groupSeparator apostrophe, an edited entry whose proposedRate is "1234.56789" reads Edited from 1’234,567890 on its rate line and in its recording's price column, and one whose proposedRate is "0.12345678" reads Edited from 0,12345678. A figure typed over a proposal of "1234.56789", before any save, reads Edited from 1’234,567890 on its line, and so does a stored proposed entry at that rate once its line is changed

untouchedRateLine.value: a rate field prefills through editable at six places and compares by value, never by text. Its parseFigure reading equals the stored or proposed rate whenever padding is all that differs, so an untouched line writes nothing and keeps its provenance

chipOverflow.value: a chip never exceeds its container, and its text wraps rather than clipping or truncating, so a provenance is always shown in full

rateLinesBreakpoint.value: 720px, measured on the width of the rate-lines block and not of the window. At 720px or wider the lines keep the rows' columns: unit at the left, figure in the field column, provenance chip in the control column, the control column widening for a long chip on every line at once so no field falls out of line. Below 720px the lines stack: the unit's name with its pair, then the field at full width, then the provenance chip beneath it, in full

singleHoldingPricesLineLayout.value: opened, the rate lines always stack, because the Dialog's content box is 416px, below the 720px breakpoint

phoneRateLines.value: no rule of its own at phone width: the rate lines stack by the breakpoint rule above

fixtures: a seeded vault holding two accounts measured in USD, one in XAU-ozt, one in the main currency, and one in a free-text unit, which is the spread every refresh rule turns on

rate lines whose unit has a long full name and whose provenance is the longest of the three renderings (an edited rate naming a long replaced figure, and a proposal with an 'as of' day), laid out in a block just under and just at 720px wide, and in the 416px single-holding dialog

a recording date holding an entry the person edited a year ago, for the assertion that opening it neither refetches nor restamps
two planted entries for one (symbol, date) with different rate strings, and a second pair whose decrypted payloads are byte-identical, supplied to the client in both orders
an export and import round trip over the planted differing pair, since version resets to 1 and any ranking that consulted it would read differently on either side
a lookup: false symbol and a free-text unit each holding one previous entry, for the two no-rate-source cases, which look different and must behave alike
request-capture over the full outbound request including headers, for the assertion that no edited rate, quantity or account identifier reaches /api/rates

a holding archived on a date that holds a recording with a complete set of price entries, and one archived on a date that holds none, for the archive-is-recording assertions (the criteria are spec/features/manage-accounts.md#acceptance-criteria)
a price entry on a date where one holding is archived with its zero and another holding in the same unit holds a figure, for the confirmation count that leaves the zero out

a USD holding with a snapshot at 2010-03-31 and USD entries at 2010-03-31 only, a date at 2026-04-10 holding no records, a variant of that date holding a complete set of entries, and a variant missing exactly one symbol, for the move assertions and the price at a date
a free-text unit and a lookup: false symbol, each with its only entry at 2024-01-15, for the price at a date carrying 2024-01-15 at 2026-04-10, none date at 2024-01-15 and none at 2024-01-14

an XAU-g unit with entries at 2011-06-30, typed, and 2013-01-02 only, for the price at a date at 2012-12-31 (the 2011-06-30 entry, carrying 2011-06-30), 2011-06-29 (none) and 2013-01-03 (none), and a sweep at 2012-12-31 whose only unit without an entry is XAU-g, in one variant with an XAU-g entry at or before the date and one without

a vault with main currency BRL holding a USD figure, whose symbol table rows give USD and BRL their since values, for USD having a rate source at 2000-01-13 and none at 2000-01-12, with a USD entry at or before 2000-01-12
an archived holding whose entry sits before its archive date, in a unit with no entry at the earlier date it is moved to, for the moved entry's own unit being refreshed
a stubbed rate PUT that fails during a move, and a stubbed snapshot PUT that fails, for the move's write order and its report

a sweep at a date holding no record, with USD proposed and a price typed on a free-text unit's line, the date empty of snapshots and rates both, for the typed-price-waits assertions: the control's absence, the direct call to the client's rate-lines write, leaving with no row recorded, and recording the first row. A stub counting every PUT and DELETE to /api/records over the flow

locale de-DE with groupSeparator apostrophe, and edited entries whose proposedRate is "1234.56789" and "0.12345678", plus a stored proposed entry at "1234.56789" whose line is changed and a figure typed over that proposal before any save, for the Edited from assertions on the rate line and in the recording's price column
a stored rate of "0.9312" on a reopened recording, whose line prefills 0.931200, for the untouched-line assertion with the record captured before and after

a sweep open on a recording whose rate lines include one with no entry (so a save creates one), and a second session that deletes every record at that date before the save, for the emptied-date assertions
focus: clearing every quantity at a date must leave that date's rate entries byte-identical and the recording still reopenable with its rate lines. This is easy to satisfy on paper and easy to fake with a test that only checks the recording still appears, so the rate rows have to be compared byte for byte and the symbols shown still pricing the dates around the cleared date

nothing in the vault may record that a save was partial. A reviewer has to look for the absence of a pending flag or dirty marker in the stored records after a half-failed save, not only for the message on screen. An implementation that quietly writes one is invisible to every behaviour test

the refresh must write price entries when the only row recorded is a main-currency account. That is the case the whole split exists for and it is the one a naive implementation skips, because nothing about that row needs a rate

one rate request per sitting, not per row. A fifteen-row sweep that fans out per symbol still writes exactly the right entries and passes every data assertion, so the request count has to be asserted directly

no request to /api/rates may carry an edited rate, a quantity or an account identifier, asserted over the full request including headers and query string. Checking the documented parameter set is not the same as checking what was actually sent

opening a recording of any age, one with an empty rate line included, must issue no request to /api/rates and write no record. The fakeable version checks only the proxy. The assertion that matters covers every PUT and DELETE in the flow as well, over a date whose provider figure has since been revised

Look it up must be asserted as a request count and a position: none on opening, exactly one on pressing it, for the line's date, and no record written until the rate-lines save. It must be absent on a line that holds an entry and on a line whose symbol has no rate source, free text and lookup: false separately. An implementation that fetches on open and renders the answer on press passes any end-state check

the Edited from figure must be asserted on all four places it appears (the rate line, the recording's price column, a figure typed over a proposal before any save, and a stored proposed entry once its line is changed) with a proposedRate of more than six places. A formatter that rounds to six passes the 1’234,567890 case and writes 0,123457 for 0.12345678, naming a figure nobody proposed

a rate line prefilled as 0.931200 from a stored 0.9312 and saved untouched must write no record and keep rateSource, asserted by comparing the stored record before and after. A comparison by text sees a change in the padding and restamps the entry as edited

editing an edited entry a second time must leave proposedRate at the original proposal. An implementation that captures the currently displayed figure each time passes the first edit and silently loses the provider's number on the second

the differing-duplicate pair must resolve identically on two clients given the records in either order and identically before and after an export and import round trip. A ranking that reads version or updated_at passes a single-client test and fails both of these

a symbol with no rate source and an existing entry must write no new entry, asserted for a free-text unit and for a lookup: false symbol separately, because the second one looks listed and is the one an implementation treats as an outage

a price typed at a date holding no record must be asserted to write nothing until the first quantity: typing it shows no rate-lines save, leaving the sweep issues no PUT and no DELETE and the landed screen names the unit, and recording the first row writes the snapshot, then the typed unit's entry as manual and the proposed one as proposed. The client's rate-lines write must also be called directly at that date and shown to issue no request, because hiding the control passes every test that goes through the UI, and the check is against the model in memory, before any request

the emptied-date state must be asserted with a second session deleting every record at the date after the sweep opened on it, and a save that creates a price: the save issues its reload and no PUT and no DELETE, the typed prices are still in their fields afterwards, the rows read as nothing recorded, no save control shows, the Callout carries the critical icon and the copy, and recording the first row then writes the typed price. A save that quietly recreates the recording, or clears what was typed, passes every test that only looks for the message

the write order inside the rate-lines save has to be asserted on the wire: every rate PUT before any DELETE. A test that only checks the end state passes whatever order was used, and the order is the whole of the guarantee

the rate lines' layout has to be asserted on rendered geometry, not on class names: no chip's box wider than its container, no two elements' boxes intersecting, no scrollWidth beyond clientWidth, and the full provenance text present in the DOM and visible. Run it on the opened prices line of the single-holding form at a phone width and a desktop width, where it must stack at both

the 720px switch belongs to the rate-lines block, not to the window. A viewport media query passes at the sweep's own widths and fails where the block is narrower than the window, so assert it with the block at 719px and at 720px under the same viewport

the archive's refresh must run before the archive flag, while the holding is still active, so the archived holding's own unit is priced at the archive date. A refresh run after the flag passes every sweep test and leaves the last holding in a unit with no price at its own archive date

a refresh that is an ensure must rewrite no entry on an archive onto a date that already holds a recording, compared record by record before and after, and a retry after a failed flag must rewrite none it already wrote

the edit confirmation's count must leave out a holding at zero on that date and a holding archived on it, asserted against a unit shared with a holding that holds a figure. A count of every holding in the unit passes a single-holding fixture

a move must be asserted as a refresh: moving a USD snapshot from 2010-03-31 to an empty 2026-04-10 issues exactly one request to /api/rates, for 2026-04-10, and writes an entry there for every symbol the refresh covers, with every entry at 2010-03-31 byte-identical. Moving onto a date with complete prices must issue no request and leave every entry at it byte-identical, and onto a date missing one symbol write that symbol only. An implementation that moves the quantity and leaves the new date unpriced passes every other move test

with the proxy answering No Content for a move, the entry must read not priced at the new date, never at the 2010-03-31 rate. A fallback to the nearest earlier entry looks priced and is the exact fault the rule exists to prevent

the move's request order must be asserted on the wire, snapshot PUT then every rate PUT then the DELETE, with the snapshot PUT stubbed to fail (no rate PUT and no DELETE issued) and with a rate PUT stubbed to fail (the DELETE still runs and the dialog names the symbol). Changing only a value or a note must issue no request to /api/rates and write no rate record

the price at a date must be asserted for a symbol with a rate source holding only an earlier entry (not priced, never the earlier entry) and for a symbol without one (the earlier entry, carrying its date), on the recording, the holding's list and the sweep's converted figure. A single fallback rule for both passes one half and fails the other

the rate source test must be asserted on the date and not only on the symbol: XAU-g at 2012-12-31 has none and at 2013-01-02 has one, and with main currency BRL, USD has one at 2000-01-13 and none at 2000-01-12, taking the newest USD entry at or before 2000-01-12. A test of lookup: true alone passes an implementation that asks the proxy about gold in 2012, and one that ignores the quote's since passes every CHF vault

a sweep at 2012-12-31 whose only unit without an entry is XAU-g must issue no request to /api/rates, show the newest earlier entry and never the wording of a source that did not answer, and write no XAU-g entry unless the line was changed, in which case it writes one as manual. With no entry at or before the date, recording an XAU-g row makes the line ask for a price and the snapshot is still written. Asserted on the request count and the record sets, not on the screen

a no-rate-source symbol writing no new entry must also be asserted for XAU-g at 2012-12-31, beside free text and lookup: false, since it has a source on later dates and is the one an implementation treats as an outage
